Name: hole_backfill_static_counterfactual
Title: Which Counterfactual Is Item Credit? Hole, Backfill and Static-Exemplar Replacement Give Different Per-Item Values for Retrieved Experience, and Only Backfill Predicts What Pruning Realizes
Short Hypothesis: For the same retrieved item in the same (game, seed) at the same slot, three references give three different credits: hole (the slot left empty; what CUE-R REMOVE, Shapley-RAG and DIG estimate), backfill (the retriever's next-ranked bank item enters in rank order; exactly what pruning the item from the bank realizes for that game) and static (the type's best static exemplar takes the slot; Measurement C at item level). For natural expert items at rank 1 the backfill recovers at least 8 net of the hole loss, so hole credit over-states the realized value of pruning by at least that much; the item still carries at least 8 net beyond the static exemplar (about half of the measured set residual k3 - static3 = +17.2 sits in the top slot), giving the ordering s(H1) < s(S1) < s(B1); and summed hole credits over-predict the realized loss of pruning two items by at least 12 net, while the summed-backfill error is reported against a pre-registered +/-10 margin. The hole-backfill gap is a slot property, identical for every item class by construction, so class enters only through the credit level: a planted wrong-procedure item at rank 1 has hole credit <= -10 net even with correct co-items, and both references prune it.
Related Work: CUE-R (arxiv:2604.05467) measures per-evidence utility by REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE in single-shot RAG, replacing with distractors rather than the retriever's own next candidate, and reports no cost or variance. Shapley source attribution in RAG (arxiv:2507.04480) and DIG confidence gain (arxiv:2509.12765) are hole-based marginal contributions in single-shot QA. The local additive attribution taxonomy (arxiv:2607.14271) names the reference (what replaces the removed input) as a specification choice but does not evaluate references against a downstream decision; semantic-missingness baselines (arxiv:2508.14482) argue the reference must be a plausible state, which for a memory bank is the next-ranked item. On the agent side credit is set-level (UCOB arxiv:2606.29502; ExpSuite arxiv:2605.30712), agent-level (TreeMem arxiv:2605.04811) or write-action-level (HiMPO arxiv:2606.16285); utility-refining systems that prune (ReMe arxiv:2512.10696; SF-AMS arxiv:2607.22562) never state which counterfactual their score is meant to track. Inside the program, the nested-k logs give hole credit per slot for free and Measurement C (runs/STEP0_RESULTS.md) fixes the best static arm (static3, three type-conditioned exemplars) and its set-level residual k3 - static3 = +17.2; nothing gives the backfill counterfactual, and no measurement puts the static content into a single slot with retrieved co-items present.
Abstract: Every memory system that prunes or admits items acts on a per-item score, but the score is validated (when at all) against removing the item and leaving a hole, whereas pruning realizes a different counterfactual: the retriever fills the slot with its next-ranked item. We measure, for the rank-1 item of the same ALFWorld (game, seed) with a Qwen3-32B reader over k=3 expert-bank sets, three references for the same slot: hole (k=2), backfill (the rank-4 item from the same k=7 retrieval log, in rank order, which is exactly what pruning that item from the bank re-retrieves for that game because retrieval is deterministic) and static (the static3 type-conditioned exemplar in the slot, Measurement C at item level). Each reference costs one re-run per (game, seed), the same as leave-one-out; 274 games x 6 seeds give +/-5 net on every two-arm paired contrast. Credits are reported under two co-retrieved-set compositions (natural, and with item 2 removed or pruned), for two item classes at the same slot (natural expert, planted wrong-procedure) with the shared counterfactual arms made explicit, and additivity is tested by pairwise versus single removal: the summed hole credits of items 1 and 2 are compared with the realized loss of pruning both (backfilled by items 4 and 5). The contribution is a statement of what per-item credit is for: the reference that equals what pruning realizes, its distance from hole credit and from static credit in net points, its additivity, its reader-dependence (separate consumer-swap arm), and the number of seeds a stable per-item rank needs under each reference.
Experiments: Unit: (game, seed) over the 274 valid_seen + valid_unseen games; 6 seeds for the core arms (1,644 units: +/-5 net on a two-arm paired contrast, +/-7 on a four-arm contrast), 4 seeds for the secondary arms (1,096 units: +/-5.7 / +/-8). Sets come from the k=7 logs in runs/sweep/k_sweep_final.jsonl (item ids in rank order; retrieval is deterministic, so removing items from the bank and re-retrieving for that game yields the next-ranked items in rank order, and the frozen log realizes per-game pruning exactly). Arms on natural expert sets, prompt order = rank order: F = [1,2,3]; H1 = [2,3]; B1 = [2,3,4]; S1 = [x,2,3] with x = the game's type-conditioned static3 exemplars, as many (1-3) as fall within 15% of item 1's token count (trimmed at a step boundary if needed; token ratio logged); H2 = [1,3]; B12 = [3,4,5]; H12 = [3]; B2 = [1,3,4]; F_w1 = [w,2,3] with w = item 1 with its procedure action swapped (heat<->cool, clean->heat) or its target receptacle swapped (pick types, look-in-light), token count within 5% of item 1. Credits c_X(p) = s(F) - s(X_p) paired by (game, seed); slot values g_1 = s(B1) - s(H1), sigma_1 = s(S1) - s(H1). Composition: c_H(1) is reported under [.,2,3] (F vs H1) and under [.,3] (H2 vs H12); c_B(1) under [.,2,3] (F vs B1) and under [.,3,4] (B2 vs B12). Pairwise vs single: hole sum c_H(1)+c_H(2) versus the realized two-item pruning loss s(F) - s(B12) (P3) and versus the pairwise hole c_H(12); backfill sum c_B(1)+c_B(2) versus s(F) - s(B12) (estimand D_B, margin +/-10). Class: F_w1 versus the same H1/B1 prompts (identical for every class; stated as such). Consumer swap: H1 and B1 re-run on the second local backbone (serving verified before the cell is scheduled). Budget: 6 arms x 1,644 (F, H1, B1, S1, H2, B12) = 9,864; 3 arms x 1,096 (H12, B2, F_w1) = 3,288; swap 2 arms x 1,096 = 2,192; total 15,344 episodes = 12.8 h at the measured 20 episodes/min on two vLLM replicas (one per A100, prefix caching on, episode workers raised until each replica's running queue stays >= 8), plus about 2% error re-runs; every arm is an append-only JSONL under nohup with a pid file. Order: F and H1 on seeds 1-4 first as the positive control (c_H(1) >= +10 at +/-5.7; if it fails, the pre-registered fallback makes the pair {1,2} the primary slot, with g_12 = s(B12) - s(H12) carrying P1 and the single-slot cells reported as exploratory); pre-registration of all thresholds filed before B1 starts; the remaining arms are interleaved across both replicas so neither GPU idles. If the confirmatory arms finish under budget, a bank-level realization arm R1 (prune every validation rank-1 item from the bank, re-retrieve, 1,644 episodes) runs on the remaining time as a fidelity estimand for s(B1) - s(R1); it carries no confirmatory prediction.
Baselines and Ablations: Nested-k slot credit from the existing logs (k=1 vs k=3 vs k=7) as the free position-level prior, which says items 4-7 add only +2 to +4 net on top of [1,2,3] and against which P1 is stated; k=1 leave-one-out excluded because it equals the k=0 contrast; hole vs backfill vs static as a within-unit factorial at the rank-1 slot; composition as a manipulated factor (each rank-1 credit under two co-sets: natural, and with item 2 removed or pruned); pairwise removal vs single removal for both references (P3 and the D_B estimand); class (natural expert vs planted wrong-procedure) at the same slot with the shared counterfactual arms made explicit; the static3 exemplar in the slot as the item-level Measurement C arm, with the set-level static3 numbers as the reference; backfill-to-removed-item similarity (embedding cosine, same-object flag, same-receptacle flag) as a covariate for g_1, separating near-duplicate backfills from distinct ones; per-type breakdown (clean/heat/cool vs pick types vs look-in-light) reported, not confirmatory; second backbone as a separate consumer-swap arm; seeds as a factor; split-half rank stability across seeds as the noise estimand.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (backfill differs from hole at rank 1; the mechanism): g_1 = s(B1) - s(H1) >= +8 net, i.e. the retriever's next candidate placed in the emptied rank-1 slot recovers at least 8 net of the hole loss, so hole credit over-states the value that pruning the item realizes by at least 8 net. Stated against the nested-k prior (items 4-7 add +2 to +4 on top of the full set). Falsified if g_1 <= 0 with the 95% CI excluding +8 (the next-ranked item adds nothing to [2,3]: hole credit is what pruning realizes and the reference does not matter). Arms: H1 vs B1, 1,644 paired, CI +/-5, MDE 7, band 8. The ratio c_B(1)/c_H(1) is reported with a bootstrap CI as an estimand under the gate c_H(1) >= +10, not as a target.
- P2 (class enters through the level, not the gap): for a planted wrong-procedure item at rank 1, c_H(w1) = s(F_w1) - s(H1) <= -10 net even though items 2-3 carry the correct procedure (the reader follows the top-ranked procedure). Falsified if c_H(w1) >= 0 with the CI excluding -10 (the correct co-items dominate and the wrong item is ignored). Arms: F_w1 vs H1 on seeds 1-4, 1,096 paired, CI +/-5.7, band 10. Because H1 and B1 are the same prompts for every class, c_B(w1) = c_H(w1) - g_1 is an identity (both references prune the item) and is not a prediction.
- P3 (headline: which reference predicts realized multi-item pruning): the summed hole credits of items 1 and 2 over-predict the realized loss of pruning both, which the retriever backfills with items 4 and 5: D_H = [c_H(1) + c_H(2)] - [s(F) - s(B12)] = s(F) + s(B12) - s(H1) - s(H2) >= +12 net. Falsified if D_H <= 0 with the 95% CI excluding +12 (pruning two items realizes at least what their holes sum to: a hole-based pruner is calibrated). Arms: F, H1, H2, B12, all 1,644 paired, four-arm CI +/-7, band 12. The backfill-sum error D_B = s(F) + s(B12) - s(B1) - s(B2) is reported with its CI (1,096 paired, +/-8) against a pre-registered equivalence margin of +/-10 net (TOST, 90% CI); it is an estimand of backfill additivity, not a confirmatory prediction.
- P4 (item value net of the static arm; Measurement C at slot level): c_S(1) = s(F) - s(S1) >= +8 net, i.e. the rank-1 item carries at least 8 net beyond the type's best static exemplar in the same slot with the same co-items; stated against the measured set-level residual k3 - static3 = +17.2 (+/-5): about half of it sits in the top slot. Falsified if c_S(1) <= 0 with the CI excluding +8 (the static exemplar substitutes for the retrieved item once co-items carry the procedure: slot credit is procedure credit). Arms: F vs S1, 1,644 paired, CI +/-5, band 8; the ordering s(H1) < s(S1) < s(B1) is reported with CIs on sigma_1 and g_1 - sigma_1.
- P5 (consumer swap, separate arm): on the second backbone g_1' = s(B1') - s(H1') >= +8 net (the backfill gap is a property of the bank's redundancy, not of the reader). Falsified if g_1' <= -2 with the CI excluding +8 (the second reader gets nothing from the next-ranked item: the gap is reader-specific). Arms: H1', B1' on backbone 2, 1,096 paired, CI +/-5.7, band 10; stated as a difference in net points, not a ratio of ratios.
Measurement and Noise Control: All contrasts paired by (game, seed); cluster bootstrap over games with seed as a factor; measured floors +/-8 net at 548 paired, +/-5.7 at 1,096, +/-5 at 1,644 for a two-arm contrast, times sqrt(2) for a four-arm contrast (+/-8 and +/-7); every prediction band is at least 1.6x the relevant half-width and each states its MDE. Between-seed SD of each arm's success rate and of each credit is reported. Per-item rank stability is an estimand: per-game c_H(1) and c_B(1) are computed on seeds 1-3 and 4-6, the split-half Spearman over 274 games is reported and Spearman-Brown-extrapolated to the number of seeds needed for rho >= 0.5; that number times 274 is the episode cost of a stable per-item rank under each reference. Estimator cost: every reference costs exactly one re-run per (game, seed), the same as leave-one-out (one reference at +/-5 = 1,644 episodes = about 82 min on two replicas); backfill and static need no extra retrieval or generation (the k=7 log and the static3 exemplars are on disk), so no arm needs more re-runs than the leave-one-out baseline. Gate: c_H(1) >= +10 on seeds 1-4 before B1 is scheduled; ratios are interpreted only under the gate, net-point predictions do not depend on it, and the fallback slot is pre-registered. Equivalence statements (D_B, and s(B1) - s(R1) if R1 runs) use TOST with 90% CIs and pre-registered margins (+/-10, +/-6). Prompt hashes and token counts of every replacement are logged (static replacements within 15%, wrong-procedure edits within 5% of the replaced item's tokens); retrieval is frozen from the logs so no confirmatory arm re-retrieves; per-type results reported but only pooled claims are confirmatory; both GPUs busy: one vLLM replica per A100, prefix caching on, workers tuned so each replica's running queue stays >= 8, throughput (episodes/min, tok/s per GPU) reported with every status update.

Risk Factors and Limitations: c_H(1) may fall below +10 if same-type co-items make the top item redundant; then per-item credit at k=3 is below the floor (a finding in itself) and the pre-registered fallback moves the primary slot to the pair {1,2}. Backfill items can be near-duplicates of item 1, which is the mechanism but makes c_B(1) small; the similarity covariate separates near-duplicate from distinct backfills. Static3 exemplars are about 143 tokens each, so token matching uses 1-3 exemplars and is approximate. Wrong-procedure edits are template edits of one action and may be partly self-corrected by the reader. The hole-backfill gap is by construction class-independent, so this design can say nothing about class x reference interactions beyond credit levels; a design that could would need class-specific counterfactual content, which does not exist for a removed item. Per-game pruning is realized exactly by the frozen-log backfill; a bank-level pruning policy additionally couples games through shared items, and that coupling (R1) is measured only if time remains. Second-backbone serving is unverified. Results are ALFWorld-specific: six task types with strong procedure sharing may make g_1 larger than in environments whose trajectories carry instance-specific content.
Addresses gap: G5 (single-shot RAG intervention attribution has not been extended to multi-step agents with a persistent bank, and whether item credit transfers to the decision that uses it is untested); secondarily G1 (no per-item counterfactual exists inside an agentic memory system).
Not a restatement of: Brief bullet 'Marginal value of items 2-3 over item 1 = +7 net; of items 4-7 = +4' (nested-k slot credit): that bullet measures the value of a slot under hole removal in nested sets; this idea claims the value of a specific item relative to its backfill is a different and smaller quantity, predicts g_1 >= 8 where the nested-k prior says +2 to +4, and tests which reference predicts a realized two-item pruning. Digest card arxiv:2604.05467 (CUE-R REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE): that card replaces with distractors in single-shot RAG; this idea replaces with the retriever's own next candidate and with the type's static exemplar in a multi-step agent, tests additivity by pairwise removal, and reports cost and seeds-to-stable-rank. Measurement C (set-level static3 vs k3 = +17.2): that measurement swaps the whole prompt; this idea puts the same static content in one slot with retrieved co-items present and asks how much of the set residual the top slot carries. Archived memory_item_value_reliability (6.12) claimed item value is context-dependent without an intervention arm; here every value is an intervention on the same (game, seed) and the dependence is on the counterfactual's reference and on the co-set, both manipulated.
Changes made:
- P1: ratio restated as the net-point slot value g_1 = s(B1) - s(H1) >= +8 with MDE 7 at 1,644 paired (6 seeds at rank 1 instead of 2 seeds pooled over positions); no longer collapses at the gate value; stated against the nested-k prior, which predicts the opposite.
- P2: the class x reference gap withdrawn because with shared H1/B1 prompts it is identically zero for every class, and class-specific H/B arms would be the same prompts re-sampled (the suggested fix would only add noise); replaced by a level prediction c_H(w1) <= -10 (band 10 at +/-5.7) with the identity c_B(w1) = c_H(w1) - g_1 stated explicitly; self-written and cross-type classes cut because they carried no open prediction.
- P3 (headline): random bank pruning at 50/75% replaced by exact per-game two-item pruning realized from the frozen k=7 log (B12 = [3,4,5]); the claim is one four-arm contrast D_H >= +12 (CI +/-7 at 1,644, band 1.7x); backfill additivity demoted to a reported estimand with a pre-registered +/-10 margin because a +/-5 equivalence is not establishable at this noise; bank-level R1 kept only as an optional fidelity estimand.
- P4: per-type clean/heat/cool cell cut; the static reference is now the measured best static arm's own exemplars (static3) in the slot, pooled over types at 1,644; the prediction is item value net of static, c_S(1) >= +8, stated against k3 - static3 = +17.2 as the brief requires. The original ordering (static recovers two thirds of hole credit) was reversed because Measurement C already shows retrieval beats the static arm by +9.1 at k=1; the revised claim is sharper against the nested-k prior, not safer.
- P5: ratio-of-ratios replaced by the same net-point contrast on the second reader (g_1' >= +8, falsified at <= -2, band 10), H1'/B1' only, 1,096 paired per arm (was 548), at the same slot as the primary.
- Grid: single-slot cells at positions 2-3, the bare placebo arm P (Measurement C's blind1 = -3 already bounds it) and two planted classes cut; seeds raised from 2 to 6 on the six core arms; composition and pairwise-vs-single tests obtained from the same arms without new ones; total 15,344 episodes / 12.8 h (was 14,800 / 12.5 h), arithmetic stated arm by arm; split-half seeds-to-stable-rank and per-reference re-run cost added as estimands.
- Kept sharp: hole > static > backfill for expert items and 'hole sums over-predict realized pruning' remain quantitative (8, 8 and 12 net) against a program prior that predicts near-zero gaps; nothing was hedged into a measurement study.
